Cyril of Alexandria
SIR-il of al-eg-ZAN-dree-uh
proper noun
From the Greek Kürillos (“lordly,” “masterful”), a diminutive of kürios, “lord.” He is styled “of Alexandria” from the great Egyptian see he held (c. 412–444), successor to his uncle Theophilus.

See also: Cyril of Alexandria

📖 Biblical Definition

Cyril of Alexandria stands among the foremost defenders of the true doctrine of the Person of Christ, that in the incarnate Lord there is not a mere conjunction of two loosely-joined persons but one Person, the eternal Son, who took our nature into union with Himself. When Nestorius, patriarch of Constantinople, shrank from confessing that the One born of the virgin was very God, refusing her the title Theotokos (God-bearer) rightly understood as safeguarding the deity of her Son, Cyril contended against him and prevailed at the Council of Ephesus in 431. That the child in the manger was no other than the Word made flesh, John 1:14, that He who suffered was the Lord of glory, 1 Corinthians 2:8 — this Cyril laboured to establish, and the church confessed it after him at Chalcedon. His writings upon the unity of Christ’s Person, and upon the Gospel of John, remain a rich mine of Christological truth. Yet the same hand that guarded the deity of Christ also pressed the honour of His mother beyond what Scripture warrants, sowing seed that would ripen into the Marian corruptions of Rome; and his patriarchate was stained by the factional violence of Alexandria. We honour his Christ, and we mark his errors, that we may hold the one and refuse the other.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Fifth-century patriarch of Alexandria who defended the unity of Christ’s Person against Nestorius at Ephesus, though marred by Marian excess and factional violence.

CYRIL OF ALEXANDRIA, proper noun. A bishop of the Egyptian church, patriarch of Alexandria from about 412 to 444.

The principal opponent of Nestorius and champion of the one Person of the incarnate Son at the Council of Ephesus, 431.

Author of extensive commentaries, especially upon the Gospel of John, and of dogmatic treatises on the unity of Christ.

A teacher whose Christology the church received, yet whose devotion to the virgin outran Scripture and prepared Marian error.

A patriarch whose administration was disfigured by the factional and mob violence of his city.

📖 Key Scripture

Joh 1:14 — "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth."

1Co 2:8 — "Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory."

Col 2:9 — "For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily."

Heb 1:3 — "Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A defender of Christ’s Person whose later Marian excess and factional violence must be named plainly as error.

expand to see more

Cyril’s labour for the unity of Christ’s Person is honourable and true, and the church rightly received it. But his exaltation of the virgin, though it began as a guard upon the deity of her Son, was pressed beyond the warrant of Scripture, feeding a devotion to Mary that Rome would afterward inflate into invocation, mediation, and immaculate conception — corruptions that rob the one Mediator, Christ Jesus, of His sole glory, 1 Timothy 2:5. This is not a difference of emphasis to be smoothed over; it is error, and the Reformation’s recovery of Christ as the alone Advocate was recovery from precisely such corruption.

His patriarchate, further, was marked by the factional and mob violence of Alexandria, a zeal that ran to the shedding of blood and the crushing of rivals rather than the meekness of wisdom that is from above, James 3:17. Faithfulness to the truth of Christ never sanctifies the works of the flesh in its defence; the servant of the Lord must not strive, but be gentle unto all men, 2 Timothy 2:24. We hold his Christology and we reject both his Mariology and his violence, honouring what is honourable and naming error error.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

That the child of the manger is very God, one Person, the Word made flesh — and that no defender is above correction.

expand to see more

The one born of the virgin is the eternal Son, God of God, who took our nature into personal union with Himself.

He who suffered upon the cross was the Lord of glory; the fulness of the Godhead dwelt in Him bodily.

To guard the deity of Christ is honourable; to exalt His mother beyond Scripture is corruption, however it begins.

The truth of Christ is never advanced by the violence of the flesh, for the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

We may honour a teacher’s doctrine and refuse his errors, proving all things and holding fast that which is good.

Usage

"Cyril’s stand at Ephesus secured the confession that the One born of Mary is very God."

"The Reformation recovered Christ as the sole Mediator from the Marian excess that Cyril’s devotion helped to seed."

"We honour Cyril’s Christology while naming his factional violence and Mariology as error, not tradition."
